sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell a Johnson City house?
sections.html:
For speed, a buyer who pays cash and takes the house as is beats a listing, because it skips lender approval, the appraisal and rounds of repair talks. A traditional listing suits owners with no deadline who want exposure to the widest range of buyers.

Johnson City combines a university, a large hospital sector and a big rental market, so a house may appeal to an owner-occupant, a landlord or a renovator. That mix helps when yours needs work.

  • Hire an agent if the house shows well and you can wait for financing to clear.
  • Sell directly if you already have a buyer and only need a closing agent.
  • Choose a cash offer for a firm date or to avoid funding repairs.

sections.h2: What should I know about Johnson City before selling?
sections.html:
The city sits in an Appalachian valley at roughly 1,634 feet, mostly in Washington County with pieces in Carter and Sullivan counties. It began in 1856 as Johnson's Depot, a rail stop, and incorporated in 1869. Three rail lines crossed downtown, among them the Clinchfield Railroad and the narrow gauge line nicknamed Tweetsie.

Medicine and education carry the economy today. East Tennessee State University enrolls about 16,000 students, and Ballad Health, the region's largest health system, is based here. Johnson City Medical Center holds a Level 1 trauma center and Niswonger Children's Hospital. The Mountain Home veterans campus, authorized by Congress in 1901, sits across from the university.

Buffalo Mountain, a ridge above 2,700 feet, is a city park on the south side, and an arm of Boone Lake on the Watauga River reaches into the city limits. Most addresses fall in the Johnson City Independent School District, home to Science Hill High School, Indian Trail Middle and Liberty Bell Middle, though small parts of the city belong to the Washington County district. Confirm the district for your street before advertising a school zone.

Climate is humid subtropical, averaging 45.22 inches of precipitation and 15.6 inches of snow each year.

sections.h2: How do Census figures describe Johnson City homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts the city at 74,943 people on July 1, 2025, up 5.5 percent from April 2020, with 30,662 households. Among adults aged 25 and older, 42.5 percent hold at least a bachelor's degree.

  • Typical value of an owner's home: $268,200
  • Homes lived in by owners: 51.3 percent
  • Middle gross rent: $1,023
  • Middle household income: $57,254
  • Average trip to work: 18.7 minutes

About half of homes are rented and a university sits in the middle of town, so landlords belong in your buyer pool. Duplexes and houses near campus can draw extra interest.

sections.h2: What keeps Johnson City housing demand steady?
sections.html:
Wikipedia describes a Med-Tech corridor anchored by Johnson City Medical Center, Franklin Woods Community Hospital and the university's medical and pharmacy colleges, and reports a 2019 metro gross product of $9.1 billion.

Census business tallies for 2022 show $2.10 billion in health care and social assistance receipts and $2.96 billion in retail sales, or $40,793 per resident. Johnson City Transit operates 11 fixed routes and logged 386,917 trips in 2025, while Tri-Cities Regional Airport in Blountville handles flights. People who work at the hospital or campus often shop along those routes, so mention transit and commute time in your description.

sections.h2: When and how are Johnson City property taxes paid?
sections.html:
The city collects its own tax, and the Washington County Trustee collects the county's. City notices for 2026 went out the week of October 12. The balance is due February 28, 2027, with penalty and interest starting March 1, 2027.

Pay at the Municipal and Safety Building, 601 E. Main Street, between 8 and 5 on weekdays, mail a check to P.O. Box 2227, or pay online and absorb a 2.75 percent charge. The tax office answers at 423-434-6299.

The county works on a similar calendar. Its Trustee mails notices in October, accepts payment through February, and adds 1.5 percent interest to anything outstanding on March 1. The county page lists a 2023 county rate of $2.15 per $100 of assessed value and says city residents pay more on top. State law fixes the tax roll as of January 1, and the county says closings normally prorate the bill and make the buyer responsible afterward.

sections.h2: Where is a Johnson City deed filed, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Most parcels belong to the Washington County Register of Deeds in the historic courthouse at 100 E. Main Street, Jonesborough, phone 423-753-1644. The office keeps hours from 8 to 4:30 weekdays but takes no new recordings after 4 p.m. It collects the state's transfer and mortgage taxes along with filing charges.

The transfer rate is $0.37 per $100, which would come to roughly $992 on a sale at the $268,200 Census median. Washington County also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that emails you when something is filed under your name.

The city spills into Sullivan and Carter counties, so check the tax bill or call the register to learn which county holds your parcel before planning a closing.

sections.h2: Which permit and rental-tax rules affect a Johnson City sale?
sections.html:
Johnson City's Building Division issues most construction permits through its CityView portal or the counter at City Hall. A single-family owner who lives in the house may serve as general contractor and may do electrical or plumbing work after passing a free competency exam. Gas-fired mechanical work goes to a licensed mechanical contractor. Questions and inspection requests go to 423-434-6047.

Lodging is taxed. Every stay under 30 days, however booked, carries the city's 7 percent Hotel/Motel Transient Occupancy Privilege Tax, and continuous stays of 90 days or longer are exempt. Operators also collect state and local sales tax, so the total changes with the county.

Source: Johnson City Finance Department occupancy tax page; the tax specialist's number is 423-232-1480.

sections.h2: What repairs and inspections should I handle before listing?
sections.html:
The city publishes a guide to common residential inspection failures, a useful checklist before you list. Under the 2012 International Residential Code as the city cites it, a deck skips permitting only if it is no more than 200 square feet, no higher than 30 inches above grade, detached from the house and not serving a required exit. Prefabricated pools less than 24 inches deep are also exempt.

Additions, attached decks and covered porches require a site drawing and a permit. Inspection requests received by 4:30 p.m. may be scheduled for the next business day. A cash buyer may take a house with open items, while a buyer with a loan may want them resolved first.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 property tax deadline in Johnson City?
faqs.a: February 28, 2027. The city mailed notices the week of October 12, 2026, and penalty and interest begin March 1, 2027. The tax office is 423-434-6299.

faqs.q: Where is a Johnson City deed recorded?
faqs.a: Parcels in Washington County go to the Register of Deeds at 100 E. Main Street, Jonesborough, 423-753-1644, which takes no recordings after 4 p.m. Parcels in the Sullivan or Carter County parts fall under those counties' registers.

faqs.q: Can I act as my own contractor in Johnson City?
faqs.a: If you own and live in a single-family home, yes. Doing your own electrical or plumbing also requires passing a free competency exam, and mechanical work must go to a licensed contractor.

faqs.q: Which tax applies to short-term rentals in Johnson City?
faqs.a: Stays under 30 days owe the city's 7 percent occupancy tax plus state and local sales tax. The total is 16.5 percent in the Washington County portion.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a Johnson City sale?
faqs.a: The state rate is $0.37 per $100 of price, about $992 on a $268,200 sale. The sales contract decides whether the buyer or the seller pays it.
